_comment: PERFORMANCE suite: the ingestion throughput of the postgrescdc stream source -- the rows a stream publisher writes to its files per second, before a trigger makes them a manifest -- over 1000000 rows (250000 in each of the employeescdc tables accounts, ledger, devices, readings), loaded before the stream starts so it reads a backlog. The publisher (functions/perf_postgrescdc.py::postgrescdc_changes) is registered from the head: the 1000000 are changes it reads from the WAL, over the domain's own replication slot (created with the domain, so it holds every insert). STAGES: (1) domains -- create the postgrescdc domain, install employeescdc, create-data --size 2500; (2) collections; (3) functions -- register the publisher, which STARTS it; (4) execute -- scripts/cdc_throughput.py reads the stream worker's log until its files hold 1000000 rows or 10m has passed, and says rows, files, MB, seconds from the plugin's run() to the last file and rows/s in the step's note (PARTIAL when short; the step still passes); (5) monitor. Generated by gen_suites.py. Run one at a time -- lanes side by side share the machine and skew the figure: `tdd xp one-shot --suite performance/postgrescdc_changes`.
